executive_summary: Database Health Score: 5/100. Diagnostic telemetry identified 23 performance and reliability issues: 4 vacuum/bloat hotspot(s), 15 table(s) suffering high sequential scans, 4 redundant index(es) causing write amplification, and 0 table(s) with stale statistics. findings.root_cause_analysis: Severe MVCC dead tuple accumulation detected on 'public.client_session_archive' (6.99% dead tuples, 268,528 dead rows vs 3,571,891 live rows). In PostgreSQL, UPDATE and DELETE operations do not overwrite disk blocks in-place; they write new tuple versions and mark old versions as dead. Because autovacuum has not reclaimed these dead versions, the table suffers from physical heap bloat, increased disk I/O, cache pollution in shared_buffers, and degraded sequential/index scan throughput.
findings.locking_impact: Safe for production: Standard `VACUUM` takes only a ShareUpdateExclusiveLock, allowing concurrent SELECTs, INSERTs, UPDATEs, and DELETEs. It will NOT block application traffic. (Avoid VACUUM FULL, which demands an AccessExclusiveLock and locks out all queries).
